meta.title: Thai Green Curry from Scratch
meta.description: A proper Thai green curry with homemade paste, coconut cream, and Thai basil. 45 minutes, no shortcuts.

children.value: Store-bought curry paste gets you 70% of the way there. This recipe gets you to 100%. The difference is the fresh aromatics — galangal, lemongrass, and makrut lime leaves — that lose their magic the moment they hit a jar.
The Paste
This makes about ¼ cup of paste — enough for one batch of curry. It freezes well if you want to double it.
6-8 green Thai chilies (seeds in for heat, out for mild)
2 stalks lemongrass (bottom 3 inches, sliced thin)
1 thumb galangal, peeled and sliced
4 makrut lime leaves, deveined
4 cloves garlic
3 shallots
1 tsp coriander seeds, toasted and ground
½ tsp cumin seeds, toasted and ground
1 tsp shrimp paste (or 1 tbsp soy sauce for vegetarian)
Handful of cilantro roots and stems

A granite mortar and pestle makes the best paste — pounding ruptures cell walls differently than blading. But a food processor works fine for a weeknight. Add a splash of coconut cream to help it blend.
The Curry
1 can (400ml) coconut cream (not coconut milk — you want the fat)
500g protein: chicken thigh, shrimp, or firm tofu
200g Thai eggplant or regular eggplant, cubed
1 cup bamboo shoots
2 tbsp fish sauce
1 tbsp palm sugar (or brown sugar)
Big handful Thai basil leaves
2-3 makrut lime leaves, torn
Method
Scoop the thick cream from the top of the can into a cold wok or heavy pan. Heat over medium-high until it
splits
— you'll see oil separating from the solids. This takes 3-4 minutes and is the foundation of the curry's richness.
Don't skip the crack. If you dump everything in at once, you get a thin, watery curry instead of the rich, creamy sauce you're after.
Add all of the curry paste to the cracked coconut cream. Fry for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant and the oil turns green. You should be able to smell every aromatic individually.
Add your protein and stir to coat. Cook for 2-3 minutes until the outside is sealed. Don't worry about cooking it through — it'll finish in the simmer.
Pour in the remaining coconut cream (the thinner liquid from the bottom of the can). Add fish sauce, palm sugar, torn lime leaves, eggplant, and bamboo shoots. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Simmer uncovered for 8-10 minutes until the eggplant is tender and the sauce has thickened slightly. Taste and adjust: more fish sauce for salt, more sugar for sweetness, more chili for heat. Kill the heat and fold in the Thai basil — it wilts in seconds.
Serve over jasmine rice with extra basil, sliced chilies, and a squeeze of lime.
Variations
Chicken thigh + Thai eggplant + bamboo shoots. This is the standard Bangkok street version. Use bone-in thigh for maximum flavor if you don't mind picking around the bones.
Shrimp + mussels + squid. Add the seafood in the last 3-4 minutes — it cooks fast and goes rubbery if overdone. Replace bamboo shoots with baby corn.
Pressed firm tofu + sweet potato + green beans. Replace fish sauce with soy sauce + a splash of lime juice. Replace shrimp paste in the curry paste with fermented soybean paste (tao jiao).
Substitutions, ranked from best to acceptable:
Galangal
→ fresh ginger (different flavor but works)
Makrut lime leaves
→ zest of 2 limes (add at the end)
Thai basil
→ Italian basil + a few mint leaves
Palm sugar
→ brown sugar or coconut sugar
